title: Some People Keep Razor-Sharp Minds Into Their 80s and Beyond.
summary:
长期以来，神经科学家一直试图回答一个问题：成年人的大脑是否还能产生新的神经细胞（神经元）。这一过程被称为“神经发生”，在个体发育阶段至关重要，早在20世纪60年代，针对啮齿类动物的研究就曾提出，发育成熟的大脑或许也具备这种能力。此后不断积累的证据显示，包括啮齿类和非人灵长类在内的部分动物确实存在成体神经发生现象，但人类是否同样如此，至今仍是激烈争论的焦点。

来源：史密森尼；作者：Sara Hashemi；原文发布时间：2026-05-05 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: Neuroscientists have long struggled to understand whether the adult human brain spawns new nerve cells, or neurons. The process, called neurogenesis, is crucial during development, and rodent research in the 1960s hinted that the mature brain might undergo it as well. Mounting evidence since then has suggested that some animals, including rodents and nonhuman primates, experience adult neurogenesis, but humans have remained at the heart of a contentious debate.
paragraphs.contentZh: 长期以来，神经科学家一直试图回答一个问题：成年人的大脑是否还能产生新的神经细胞（神经元）。这一过程被称为“神经发生”，在个体发育阶段至关重要，早在20世纪60年代，针对啮齿类动物的研究就曾提出，发育成熟的大脑或许也具备这种能力。此后不断积累的证据显示，包括啮齿类和非人灵长类在内的部分动物确实存在成体神经发生现象，但人类是否同样如此，至今仍是激烈争论的焦点。

paragraphs.contentEn: Now, a new analysis of 38 human brains supports the idea that adults do, indeed, birth neurons—and that replenishing these cells might help preserve certain cognitive functions. In a study published February 25 in the journal Nature, adults ages 80 and older with outstanding memory—dubbed “super-agers”—had twice as many new neurons in their hippocampi, a brain region crucial for memory, as older adults with normal memory for their age, and two and a half times as many as people with Alzheimer’s disease. “This shows the aging brain has the capacity to regenerate—that’s huge,” says study co-author Tamar Gefen, a clinical neuropsychologist at Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine, to Sandee LaMotte at CNN.
paragraphs.contentZh: 如今，一项基于38例人类大脑样本的最新分析为这样一种观点提供了支持：成年人确实会产生新的神经元——这些细胞的持续补充，可能有助于维持特定的认知功能。这项于2月25日发表在《自然》期刊上的研究显示，80岁及以上、记忆力异常出色的老年人——被称为“超级老人”——其海马体（大脑中与记忆密切相关的关键区域）中新生神经元的数量，约为记忆力正常同龄老人的2倍，更是阿尔茨海默病患者的2.5倍。研究合著者、美国西北大学费恩伯格医学院临床神经心理学家塔玛·格芬在接受CNN记者桑迪·拉莫特采访时表示：“这说明，即便在衰老过程中，大脑依然具备再生能力——这太了不起了。”

paragraphs.contentEn: The human brain stays busy making new neurons during early embryonic development and infancy, but the activity sharply declines during childhood. Super-agers can recall everyday events and past personal experiences as easily as people decades younger, in their 50s, but have IQ levels comparable to those of others their age. In the study, the researchers examined donated brains from members of this special group, as well as those from four other classes: older adults with no cognitive problems, older adults with mild or early dementia, older adults with Alzheimer’s disease and younger adults ages 20 to 40 with intact memory.
paragraphs.contentZh: 在人类早期胚胎发育和婴儿阶段，大脑会持续生成大量新的神经元，但这一活动在儿童期会迅速减弱。“超级老人”能够像比他们年轻数十岁的人（例如五十多岁）一样，轻松回忆日常事件与个人过往经历，但其智商水平与同龄人基本相当。在这项研究中，研究人员对该特殊群体捐赠的大脑进行了分析，同时还纳入了另外四类人群的样本作为对照：认知功能正常的老年人、患有轻度或早期痴呆的老年人、阿尔茨海默病患者，以及记忆功能完好的20至40岁成年人。

paragraphs.contentEn: The young brains helped Gefen and her colleagues find genetic markers of several types of baby neurons, which were subsequently identified in all the older adults’ brains. However, super-agers had way more of these immature cells in their hippocampi than the other elderly people—and even some of the younger adults. What’s more, nerve cells called CA1 neurons and support cells called astrocytes seem to play important roles in super-agers’ extraordinary cognition, the researchers found. CA1 neurons help form, consolidate and retrieve memories, while astrocytes help neurons build connections with one another—which allow them to communicate—and seem to stabilize memories.
paragraphs.contentZh: 以年轻大脑样本为参照，格芬及其同事识别出了几类新生神经元的基因标志物，而这些标志物随后也在所有老年人的大脑中被检测到。不过，“超级老人”海马体中这类未成熟细胞的数量明显更多，不仅超过其他老年人——甚至高于部分年轻人。研究人员还发现，一类被称为CA1神经元的神经细胞，以及被称为星形胶质细胞的支持细胞，可能在“超级老人”卓越的认知能力中发挥关键作用。具体而言，CA1神经元有助于记忆的形成、巩固与提取；星形胶质细胞则协助神经元之间建立连接——从而实现信息传递——并似乎具有稳定记忆的功能。

paragraphs.contentEn: “What’s emerging from this study is this idea that super-agers are, in general, very distinct,” says study co-author Changiz Geula, a neuroscientist at Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine, in a statement. “The genetic programs that support brain cell survival and communication stay on in super-agers in these cells, but they’re switched off in Alzheimer’s disease.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 西北大学费恩伯格医学院神经科学家、研究合著者昌吉兹·格乌拉在一份声明中表示：“这项研究传递出的一个重要信息是，从整体来看，超级老人确实是一个极为独特的群体。支持脑细胞存活和信息传递的基因程序，在超级老人的这些细胞中仍然保持活跃，而在阿尔茨海默病患者体内，这套程序处于关闭状态。”

paragraphs.contentEn: Still, some experts have reservations. Shawn Sorrells, a neuroscientist at the University of Pittsburgh who wasn’t involved in the work, says that the new study and others that point to adult neurogenesis in humans are based on indirect evidence. “We don’t actually see one cell physically changing into the next cell,” he tells Avery Hurt at National Geographic. Additionally, each analyzed group included ten or fewer individuals, which is a major limitation, Maura Boldrini Dupont, a neuroscientist and psychiatrist at Columbia University, tells Mariana Lenharo at Nature.
paragraphs.contentZh: 不过，一些专家对此仍持保留态度。未参与该研究的匹兹堡大学神经科学家肖恩·索雷尔斯指出，这项新研究以及其他支持人类存在成体神经发生的研究，所依赖的均为间接证据。他在接受《国家地理》记者艾弗里·赫特采访时表示：“我们并没有真正观察到一个细胞在物理上转变为另一个细胞。”此外，哥伦比亚大学神经科学家兼精神病学家毛拉·博尔德里尼·杜邦在接受《自然》记者玛丽安娜·伦哈罗采访时也指出，该研究所分析的每一组样本量均不超过10人，这是一个重要局限。

paragraphs.contentEn: While the new study hasn’t settled the debate on adult neurogenesis, it has pushed forward our understanding of the human brain. The next step would be to examine the roles of the adult brain’s newborn neurons, although this would require new research techniques, study co-author Orly Lazarov, a neuroscientist at the University of Illinois Chicago, tells Nature. “What we need is functional validation of these cells, to tell what they’re doing in the human brain.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 尽管这项新研究尚未就成体神经发生的问题给出定论，但它推动了人们对人类大脑的进一步认识。芝加哥伊利诺伊大学神经科学家、研究合著者奥利·拉扎罗夫在接受《自然》采访时表示，下一步将重点探究成年人大脑中新生神经元的具体作用，不过这仍有赖于新的研究技术。“我们需要对这些细胞进行功能性验证，才能明确它们在人类大脑中实际承担的功能。”
